designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Strong, clear structure: a wide-tracked serif caps title over a 2-column grid of seven steps, ending on a single centred panel that works as a natural full stop. The roman caps / italic caption pairing is classic and well matched to the confident brush line, and the line weight stays consistent across all panels, so it holds as one ink on both tees. The repeated 'Turn around.' gives a good comic rhythm, and the drawings get tighter and rounder as the steps go on, which reads well from 3 m. Weak points: panel 7, the punchline, is drawn almost the same as panel 6 (only a tiny tick mark and a slightly different eye), so the ending lands softly. The standing dogs (1-3) are larger and heavier than the curled ones, so the visual weight drops toward the bottom. The title, set at full width, is a bit loud next to the delicate captions. On the body the captions are small and the whole print sits rather narrow and tall.
designs.fix: Make step 7 visibly different from step 6 so the payoff lands: a flatter, deflated body with the chin sunk on the paws and a clearer exhale mark (a small breath puff or longer sigh lines). That one change would also give the bottom-centre panel the weight it needs to anchor the composition.
